label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: data-desk-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Wellsford Road: what we got wrong and what we are changing

On 2 November we published an analysis of Department for Transport collision records that put Wellsford Road in Fishponds at the top of Bristol's list for injury collisions, with 41 over five years. That figure was wrong. The correct number is 23, which makes Wellsford Road sixth. We corrected the article on 6 November, but a note at the foot of a page is not an adequate account of an error this size, so here is a proper one.

What went wrong

We matched each collision record to the road it happened on. The way we joined the two datasets duplicated some collision-and-road pairs, so the same collision appeared twice in a road's tally. Eighteen duplicate entries were removed from Wellsford Road's total, mostly at the Pell Street and Kingsmere Road junctions. That is the difference between 41 and 23.

Each collision, identified by its accident index, is now counted once per road. We reran the whole citywide table after making the change, and no other road moves more than two places.

The corrected figures

Road: published 2 November / corrected / corrected rank
Wellsford Road: 41 / 23 / 6th
Kingsmere Road: 34 / 32 / 1st
Alder Hill: 31 / 31 / 2nd
Tanner's Way: 29 / 28 / 3rd
Crossfield Road: 27 / 26 / 4th
Hambrook Lane: not in our top five / 24 / 5th

These are injury collisions on roads within the city council boundary, 2021 to 2025, as before.

What this means for Wellsford Road

Twenty-three is still twenty-three. Three of those collisions were serious, and none was fatal. I am not saying the road is fine. I am saying it is not the road our article made it sound like, and the description of it as the deadliest in Bristol, which took hold locally after we published, is not something our figures ever supported.

Parents have asked whether it is safe to walk children to Wellsford Primary. A count of collisions cannot answer that on its own, and I won't pretend otherwise. What we owe you is accurate numbers, so that you can judge for yourselves.

How it was caught

A member of the Fishponds Streets Forum went through the published DfT data and could not get anywhere near 41. They were right. We should have found the error ourselves before the article went out, not after it had been read more than 48,000 times.

This was a failure of our process as a desk, not of any one person. My name is on the piece, and it is on this account too.

What we are changing

From now on, a second analyst will reproduce any ranked table independently before it is published. We will also publish the cleaned dataset and the code alongside the table, so that readers can check our work step by step instead of having to guess where a number came from. If we get something wrong again, you should be able to see why.

An apology

I am sorry. I am sorry for the worry the figure caused residents of Wellsford Road and Fishponds, and for your area being described on the strength of our mistake. The wrong number travelled much further than the correction is likely to, which is why I wanted to set this out in full.

Questions in person

The Fishponds Streets Forum has invited the Ledger to its open residents' meeting at Fishponds Library on Tuesday 17 November at 7pm. I will be there to answer questions about how this happened and what we are doing about it. If you cannot make it and would like to raise something with the Data Desk, please get in touch.

Nell Garside
Data journalist, Western Ledger
